title: Constructive Truncation, Pellet-Graeffe, and Block-Multipoint Certificates for Nearly Optimal Deterministic Integer Root Finding
abstract: We present INT-ROOTS-NEAROPT-CERT-1.0, an independently reproducible, zero-floating-point verification engine and constructive Lean 4.35.0 kernel auditing the finite-dimensional algebraic, leading-truncation, Landau-Mahler, Gaussian-shift, Pellet-Graeffe bisection, and bucketed block-multipoint mechanisms of Yansong Feng and Itamar Nir's November 3, 2026 unrefereed preprint 'Finding Integer Roots of Polynomials in Nearly Optimal Time' (arXiv:2611.04730v1, Theorems 1.1(a) and 1.1(b)). Without claiming to formalize Pan's approximate complex factorization algorithm (Theorem 3.1) or Harvey-van der Hoeven asymptotic bit-complexity bounds end-to-end, we build a four-mode exact verifier over Z, Q, Z[i], and Q[i] paired with 18 constructive Lean 4 theorems (0 sorry, 0 custom axioms, 0 Classical.choice, 0 warnings). Across 16 canonical certificates (C01-C16), we certify (i) Lemma 2.2 leading-truncation root proximity (|g(r)| < 2^d) in the d = min(n,b) < n regime plus Section 2's exact r=+-1 sharpness counterexamples (x^5+3x^4+3x^3-3x^2-3x-1 and degree-7 cubic truncation), (ii) Lemma 2.1 exact Landau-Mahler chains M(g)^2 <= ||g||_2^2 < (d+1)2^{2b} and Proposition 3.4 reciprocal pullbacks H(w) = w^d g(q + 1/w) over Q[i], (iii) Lemma 3.3 exact Gaussian-integer zero-free disk certifications (9|g(q)|^2 >= 4A_R^2, 3M_deriv <= A_R) and full Appendix A Pellet-Graeffe bisection searches (h = 2^b -> 1), and (iv) Lemma 3.5 multi-bucket block multipoint evaluation and complete Theorem 1.1(a) end-to-end root finding with exact synthetic deflation. All 16 certificates, 60 unit/forgery tests, and 37 SHA-256 hashes verify deterministically.
